elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: New 14a: "Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, TrueLink shall ..." — all three limbs are anchored to that opening trigger, so assistance, return and deletion apply after every covered expiry or termination.

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: 14a(a): "at Client's request, provide transition assistance for up to six (6) months following such expiry or termination"; the request condition is not limited to anticipated expiry and applies to any expiry or termination.

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: 14a(b): "within thirty (30) days following such expiry or termination, return all Client Content and other Client data in TrueLink's possession or control" — the 30-day clock runs from termination, not from a request.

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: 14a(c): "after such return, delete such Client Content and Client data from its systems and certify such deletion to Client in writing" — deletion and certification expressly follow return.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Same opening trigger in 14a: "Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason".

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: 14a(a) grants up to six (6) months of assistance, which exceeds the 90-day fallback floor.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: 14a(b) requires return of all Client Content and other Client data within thirty (30) days following expiry or termination in a machine-readable format.

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: Not a fallback element; the fallback checklist contains only the three items above, each of which is satisfied. (Certification is nonetheless present in 14a(c).)

reasons: Preferred level is complete: 14a covers the expiry-or-termination trigger, six months' assistance at then-current rates, 30-day return in a commonly used machine-readable format, and post-return certified deletion.

The rule is a 'missing clause' insertion, so wholly new wording can still be minimal; the drafter inserted a single concise paragraph and did not delete or alter any existing language in Sections 13 or 14 (both are rendered verbatim).

No extras beyond the checklist: no survival tail, no at-own-expense language, no added remedies, damages categories or procedures. 'in TrueLink's possession or control' and 'at Client's request' track the model language and are needed to make the return and assistance obligations operable.
Data scope is drafted broadly ('all Client Content and other Client data'), so it is not limited to selected named data types; it captures the borrower/loan data referenced in the comment.

Intent is preserved: Section 13's name-server (30 days) and hosting-environment (60 days) migration duties on Client and Client's retained ownership of domains and Client Content survive without contradiction, as does Section 14's month-end wind-down of Hosting and Support Services; 14a operates after that wind-down and creates no dangling cross-reference or undefined term ('Client Content' and the parties are defined).
Comment is compliant in tone, explains the change and cites the fallback without lecturing.
